summary:
I'll write the dashboard summary now based on the notes, staying within the allowlist and redaction rules.

I've been building out a character-forge tool for SillyTavern — a builder that interviews you about a character, drafts a card, then lints and creates it live. The milestone worth mentioning is the second one: forging from an existing character with a soul-check gate on updates, so an append-only edit skips the check but anything structural gets flagged before it overwrites 42 tests worth of behavior I'd already locked in. Getting the model to reliably ask its interview questions turned out to be its own small project — some of the roleplay-tuned models drop the formatting marker my parser expected, so the parser now falls back to a looser rule rather than silently losing an answer.

Most of the plumbing underneath is Switchboard, a small proxy that lets one GPU serve several different jobs — chat, image generation, a couple of local models — without them stepping on each other. The part I keep having to revisit is eviction: swapping a 15GB model off the card and back on costs real time, so a chunk of the recent work has been about avoiding that swap rather than making it faster — keeping the right things warm, restoring saved state instead of reloading from scratch.

On BudgetTracker I shipped the read side of a small API surface so it can answer questions about spending directly rather than needing someone to open the app and eyeball totals. The finicky part was date handling in the database layer — a couple of latent bugs where a date was being passed around as a raw string instead of a real date type, which is the kind of thing that works fine until the one query that needs to do math on it.

I've also been tightening up the tool-search side of an agent framework I run day to day — instead of handing a model every tool it might ever need, it now gets a slimmed menu, and only fetches the rest by name when it actually decides it wants them. The main tuning problem is where to draw the "always visible" line; too narrow and the model tries to call an invisible tool directly and fails, too wide and you're back to the bloat you were trying to remove.

highlights.oneLiner: Single-GPU proxy for chat/image/local models; current focus is avoiding costly model eviction/reload
Shipped a read-only API surface for spending queries; fixed latent date-as-string bugs in the DB layer
Tuning progressive tool disclosure so the model only fetches extra tools it decides it needs
